SPY.what: The 500 largest US companies, weighted by size. Tech giants make up roughly a third.
SPY.drivers: US earnings growth, Fed interest rates and the big tech names (Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple).
SPY.risk: Heavy weight in a few mega-caps; higher rates pressure valuations.

QQQ.what: The 100 largest non-financial Nasdaq companies: mostly technology and AI leaders.
QQQ.drivers: AI spending, tech earnings and long-term interest rates (growth shares are rate-sensitive).
QQQ.risk: Very concentrated in a handful of tech names; falls hardest when yields jump.

DIA.what: The 30 Dow Jones blue chips, weighted by share price, not size.
DIA.drivers: Industrial, financial and health-care earnings; less tech-heavy than the S&P 500.
DIA.risk: Price-weighting means a few high-priced shares (e.g. Goldman Sachs, UnitedHealth) move it a lot.

IWM.drivers: The US domestic economy, bank lending and interest rates: small caps carry more floating-rate debt.
IWM.risk: Higher-for-longer rates raise borrowing costs; many members are loss-making.

RSP.what: The S&P 500 with every company given the same weight.
RSP.drivers: Breadth of the US market: does well when the average company, not just mega-cap tech, is rising.
RSP.risk: Lags when a few giant tech shares lead the market.

XLK.what: US technology shares from the S&P 500: chips, software and hardware.
XLK.drivers: AI and cloud spending, chip demand and interest rates.
XLK.risk: Very concentrated in Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft; high valuations.

XLF.what: US banks, insurers, payment companies and asset managers.
XLF.drivers: Interest rates and the yield curve (bank margins), credit quality and deal-making.
XLF.risk: Recession and loan losses; a flat or inverted yield curve squeezes margins.

XLV.what: US health care: drug makers, insurers, medical devices.
XLV.drivers: Drug pipelines, an ageing population and US health policy.

XLE.what: US oil and gas producers, refiners and services (Exxon, Chevron).
XLE.drivers: The oil price first: geopolitics (Middle East, Russia), OPEC+ supply and global demand.
XLE.risk: Moves with oil; falls fast when the geopolitical risk premium unwinds.

XLY.what: US consumer discretionary: Amazon, Tesla, retailers, restaurants, autos.
XLY.drivers: Consumer spending, jobs and wage growth, credit costs.
XLY.risk: Very top-heavy (Amazon and Tesla); a slowing consumer hits it first.

XLP.what: US consumer staples: food, drinks, household goods, supermarkets.
XLP.drivers: Defensive demand; tends to hold up when the economy slows.
XLP.risk: Lags in strong bull markets; input-cost and margin pressure.

XLI.what: US industrials: aerospace, machinery, railroads, defence, transport.
XLI.drivers: Factory activity (ISM), infrastructure and defence spending, global trade.
XLI.risk: Cyclical: hit by slowdowns and tariffs.

XLB.what: US materials: chemicals, metals, mining, packaging.
XLB.drivers: Commodity prices, China and global growth, the dollar.
XLB.risk: Cyclical; a strong dollar and weak China demand hurt.

XLU.what: US utilities: electricity and gas companies.
XLU.drivers: Interest rates (bond-like dividends) and AI data-centre power demand.
XLU.risk: Rising bond yields make its dividends less attractive.

XLRE.what: US real estate: REITs (data centres, towers, warehouses, offices).
XLRE.drivers: Interest rates above all; also occupancy and rents.
XLRE.risk: Very rate-sensitive: falls when long yields rise.

XLC.what: US communication services: Meta, Alphabet, Netflix, telecoms.
XLC.drivers: Digital advertising, streaming growth and AI.
XLC.risk: Concentrated in Meta and Alphabet; regulation of big tech.

SMH.what: The largest chip companies worldwide (Nvidia, TSMC, Broadcom, AMD).
SMH.drivers: AI data-centre spending, the chip cycle and US–China export rules.
SMH.risk: Extremely volatile; concentrated in Nvidia and TSMC.

IGV.what: US software companies (Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce, Adobe).
IGV.drivers: Enterprise IT budgets, cloud and AI adoption, interest rates.
IGV.risk: High valuations; AI may disrupt some software models.

XBI.what: US biotech companies, equal-weighted (many small and mid-size).
XBI.drivers: Drug trial results, FDA approvals, takeovers and interest rates.
XBI.risk: Many loss-making companies; very rate- and funding-sensitive.

KRE.drivers: Interest rates, deposit costs, commercial property loans.
KRE.risk: Deposit flight and commercial property losses.

ITB.risk: Rising mortgage rates slow sales quickly.

JETS.what: US and global airlines and airports.
JETS.drivers: Travel demand and jet fuel prices.

ITA.what: US aerospace and defence (RTX, Boeing, Lockheed Martin).
ITA.drivers: Defence budgets, geopolitics and commercial aircraft orders.
ITA.risk: Budget cuts and Boeing production problems.

CIBR.drivers: Cyber attacks, IT security budgets and AI.

ARKK.what: ARK's actively managed disruptive-innovation fund (Tesla, Roku, Coinbase and others).
ARKK.drivers: Risk appetite, interest rates and a few big positions.
ARKK.risk: Very volatile; concentrated in loss-making growth companies.

TAN.drivers: Clean-energy policy, interest rates (projects are debt-funded) and panel prices.

BOTZ.drivers: AI and automation spending, factory investment.
BOTZ.risk: Concentrated in a few names; tech sell-offs.

URA.drivers: The uranium price and new nuclear power plans (including for AI data centres).

GDX.what: Large gold-mining companies worldwide (Newmont, Agnico Eagle, Barrick).
GDX.drivers: The gold price (miners move roughly 2–3× gold), costs and the dollar.
GDX.risk: Falls harder than gold when gold drops; mining-cost inflation.

EFA.what: Large companies in developed markets outside the US and Canada (Europe, Japan, Australia).
EFA.drivers: European and Japanese growth, and the dollar: a weaker dollar helps.
EFA.risk: A strong dollar and weak European growth.

EEM.what: Emerging-market companies (TSMC, Tencent, Samsung, India, Brazil, South Africa).
EEM.drivers: China and Taiwan tech, the dollar and commodity prices.
EEM.risk: A strong dollar, China risk and Taiwan geopolitics.

INDA.what: Large Indian companies (banks, IT services, Reliance).
INDA.drivers: India's growth, domestic investment flows and the rupee.
INDA.risk: Rich valuations; oil price (India imports oil).

EWJ.drivers: Corporate reform, the yen and Bank of Japan policy.
EWJ.risk: A sharp yen rally hurts exporters.

EWZ.drivers: Commodities, Brazil's interest rates and politics.

FXI.what: The 50 largest Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong (Tencent, Alibaba, banks).
FXI.drivers: Chinese stimulus, property and tech regulation, US–China relations.

EZA.what: South African shares, US-listed and priced in dollars (Naspers, Gold Fields, FirstRand).
EZA.drivers: The JSE plus the rand: a stronger rand lifts it in dollar terms.

STX40.JO.what: The 40 largest JSE companies (Satrix 40), weighted by free-float market value.
STX40.JO.drivers: Global miners, Naspers/Prosus (Tencent), banks and the rand.
STX40.JO.risk: Heavy in a few names (Naspers/Prosus, miners); commodity swings.

STXCAP.JO.what: The JSE All Share with each company capped at 10%.
STXCAP.JO.drivers: The whole JSE: miners, banks, retailers and industrials.
STXCAP.JO.risk: Same JSE risks with less single-stock concentration.

STXRES.JO.what: JSE resources companies (Satrix RESI): gold, PGM, coal, iron ore and diversified miners.
STXRES.JO.drivers: Metal prices (gold, platinum, iron ore, coal) and the rand: a weaker rand helps miners' rand earnings.
STXRES.JO.risk: Very cyclical; commodity price falls and mining costs.

STXFIN.JO.what: JSE financial companies (Satrix FINI): banks and insurers.
STXFIN.JO.drivers: SA interest rates, credit growth and the SA economy.
STXFIN.JO.risk: Bad debts in a weak economy; SA politics.

STXIND.JO.what: JSE industrial companies (Satrix INDI): Naspers/Prosus, retailers, telecoms, consumer brands.
STXIND.JO.drivers: Tencent (via Naspers/Prosus), SA consumer spending and offshore earnings.
STXIND.JO.risk: Heavy weight in Naspers/Prosus, so Chinese tech moves it.

STXPRO.JO.drivers: SA interest rates, office/retail occupancy and the bond yield.
STXPRO.JO.risk: Rising rates and weak SA growth.

STXDIV.JO.what: JSE shares with high expected dividend yields (Satrix Dividend Plus).
STXDIV.JO.drivers: Dividends from banks, miners and other cash-generative companies.

STXQUA.JO.what: JSE companies with high profitability, low debt and stable earnings (Satrix Quality).
STXQUA.JO.drivers: Quality companies outperform when the economy slows.

STXMMT.JO.what: JSE shares with the strongest recent price momentum (Satrix Momentum).
STXMMT.JO.drivers: Whatever is trending on the JSE.
STXMMT.JO.risk: Sharp reversals when the trend turns.

STX500.JO.drivers: The S&P 500 plus the rand: a weaker rand adds to returns.
STX500.JO.risk: US market falls and a stronger rand.

STXNDQ.JO.drivers: US tech and AI, plus the rand.
STXNDQ.JO.risk: Tech concentration and a stronger rand.

STXWDM.JO.what: Developed-world shares in rand (Satrix MSCI World): about 70% US.
STXWDM.JO.drivers: Global shares, mostly the US, plus the rand.
STXWDM.JO.risk: Global sell-offs and a stronger rand.

STXEMG.JO.what: Emerging-market shares in rand (Satrix MSCI Emerging Markets).
STXEMG.JO.drivers: China, Taiwan and India tech, plus the rand.

STXCHN.JO.what: Chinese shares in rand (Satrix MSCI China).
STXCHN.JO.drivers: Chinese stimulus and tech regulation, plus the rand.

GLD.what: Physical gold held in vaults; tracks the gold price in dollars.
GLD.drivers: Real interest rates (gold pays no interest), the dollar, central-bank buying and safe-haven demand.
GLD.risk: Rising real yields and a strong dollar.

GLD.JO.drivers: The gold price in dollars plus the rand: a weaker rand lifts it.
GLD.JO.risk: Falling gold and a stronger rand.

SLV.what: Physical silver; tracks the silver price.
SLV.drivers: Gold's direction plus industrial demand (solar panels, electronics).

NGPLT.JO.drivers: Platinum supply from SA mines, car-catalyst demand and the rand.
NGPLT.JO.risk: Weak auto demand and EV substitution.

USO.drivers: OPEC+ supply, geopolitics and global demand.
USO.risk: Futures roll costs can make it lag the spot price over time.

CPER.drivers: Global growth, China construction, electrification and AI data centres.

TLT.what: US government bonds maturing in 20+ years.
TLT.drivers: Long-term interest rates: when yields rise, TLT falls (and vice versa). Inflation and Fed expectations drive yields.
TLT.risk: Hot inflation data and Fed hikes push yields up and TLT down.

IEF.what: US government bonds maturing in 7–10 years.
IEF.drivers: Medium-term interest rates and the Fed outlook.

HYG.drivers: Credit risk appetite and the economy; also interest rates.

STXGOV.JO.drivers: SA inflation, SARB rates, the budget and the rand.
STXGOV.JO.risk: Fiscal slippage and rand weakness push yields up.
